title: Jensen Huang Overtakes Michael Dell, Nears $200 Billion Fortune
excerpt: Nvidia's CEO became the world's seventh-richest person as the chipmaker's market cap surged past $5.3 trillion on relentless AI demand
body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang overtook Dell founder Michael Dell on Forbes' real-time billionaires list on May 12, with his net worth surging to $191.5 billion — just a rounding error away from the $200 billion club currently occupied by only six people on Earth.

Huang added $5.6 billion in a single day as Nvidia shares climbed 2.4% to a record $216.61, extending a four-day rally that piled $550 billion onto the chipmaker's market capitalization. Dell, meanwhile, saw his fortune slip $2.9 billion to $191.2 billion after Dell Technologies shares dropped 5.5%.

**The AI Engine:** Nvidia's ascent is inseparable from the global race to build artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company's data center division, which now accounts for over 70 percent of revenue, posted $68.1 billion in quarterly sales in its most recent report — a 71 percent year-over-year jump driven by sovereign-AI contracts and hyperscaler orders for its Blackwell-class GPUs. Analysts expect another 78 percent revenue growth when Nvidia reports earnings on May 20.

**The Wealth Ladder:** Huang now sits seventh globally, behind Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos, Larry Ellison, Bernard Arnault, and Bill Gates. His roughly 3 percent stake in Nvidia has transformed what was a mid-tier tech fortune five years ago into one of the largest concentrations of wealth in history — all built on a company he co-founded in a Denny's restaurant in 1993.

**Why India Is Watching:** Nvidia's dominance has direct implications for India's technology sector. The company has expanded its footprint in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, hiring thousands of engineers for chip design and AI research. Indian IT services firms like Infosys, TCS, and Wipro are simultaneously threatened and energized by the AI wave — threatened because AI automates the outsourced coding work that built their empires, energized because enterprises need help deploying Nvidia-powered infrastructure. Indian IT stocks hit a three-year low this week on fears that OpenAI's new consumer venture could further disrupt the services model.

**What to Watch:** Nvidia's May 20 earnings call will be the next catalyst. Any sign of slowing data center orders could puncture the rally; a beat could push Huang past the $200 billion threshold and Nvidia's market cap past Alphabet's $4.7 trillion valuation.
